draft.title: Contracts
card: A contract is an agreement that the law will enforce. It needs four things: offer, acceptance, consideration and an intention to be legally bound.
One party offers clear terms. The other agrees to those terms without changing them.
Each side gives something of value, such as money for goods. The parties must also mean the agreement to have legal effect.
Some terms are implied by law. They apply even if the contract does not write them down.
draft.remember: A contract needs four parts, and the law can add terms the parties never wrote.

a.q: Ravi agrees to pay Chen $200 for a second-hand bike, and Chen agrees to hand it over. Which part of the contract is the $200 payment?
a.why: The $200 is what Ravi gives in return for the bike, so it is consideration. It is not the offer, because the offer is the proposal of terms, and it is not acceptance, which is agreeing to those terms.
a.clue: What does each side give in exchange?

b.q: Mia emails a shop: she offers $90 for a jacket marked $120. The shop replies, 'We will sell it for $105.' Why is there no contract yet?
opts: The shop changed the terms, so Mia's offer was not accepted
Mia did not pay any money to the shop in advance
The shop's reply did not include any written implied terms
Mia and the shop did not intend to be legally bound
b.why: Acceptance must agree to the terms without changing them. The shop named a new price, so Mia's offer was not accepted. Payment in advance is not needed to form a contract, because the card only asks that each side gives something of value.
b.clue: Did the shop agree to the terms Mia offered?

b.best: The shop changed the terms, so Mia's offer was not accepted
